summary: Sustain, summon support, and patient pressure for the long fight.

loadout.howIUseIt: I establish the Gate when I can afford the opening commitment. Keeping it present gives the rest of the fight a source of pressure beyond my own actions.
I use this to move from surviving an exchange into threatening the next one. I watch for clears before committing another setup.
I use its reach and buff prevention to make an exposed opponent stay exposed. It is strongest when they are trying to rebuild.
After the opponent has spent a defensive answer, I use Yurei to combine damage with disruption. AP pressure can stop their next chain before it starts.
I use this when I want to trade damage while reducing the opponent’s next hit. It keeps a committed exchange from becoming one-sided.
I pair pressure now with healing on the following round. It is useful when I can survive the response and let the delayed recovery matter.
This lets me attack while establishing absorb for the next exchanges. I value the protection before I am already in trouble.
When the opponent has an immediate threat, I use this to reduce damage given and establish absorb. I use the extra reach to stabilise without chasing.
I use the pool drain to force an uncomfortable answer. If it draws an early cleanse, my later pressure has a much clearer path.
This is a setup tool, not a button to press on cooldown. I use it when I have a credible follow-up and enough room to survive the reply.
This is another way to make a dangerous exchange manageable. I look at the ground pattern and enemy position before choosing it.
I use this to suppress the opponent’s recovery while reducing the damage I take. I am buying a better sustained exchange, not adding a direct damage hit.

strategy.philosophy: The plan is sustain plus pressure. I am not racing for the earliest possible win. I want the opponent to fight through my protection while their resources and comfortable answers gradually disappear.
strategy.coreLoop:
Establish the Gate when the opening is safe. Maintain absorb where possible, then use Water-based support to remain in the fight while continuing to apply pressure.

When the opponent has spent a key defensive answer, turn that defensive footing into a committed offensive sequence.
strategy.opening: My first priority is to understand what the opponent can threaten immediately. If I can safely establish the Gate, I do. If not, I stabilise the exchange before spending that commitment.
strategy.defense: Absorb is most valuable when it is present across the exchanges I actually take. I combine it with healing and damage reduction, and I avoid assuming any single layer makes me safe from a full setup.
strategy.pressure: Phantom Requiem makes the opponent decide whether to tolerate pool pressure or spend a cleanse earlier than they want. I watch that decision closely. A used defensive answer can be more valuable than an extra isolated hit.
strategy.synergies: Chakra Overflow is the bridge into offense. I use it when Possessing Yurei or Aqua Dragon Barrage has a useful follow-up window, rather than treating the buff as automatic damage. The summon’s current contribution also changes which exchange I want.
strategy.matchups: Against burst, keep a defensive answer available and do not overcommit just to establish the Gate. Against recovery, use healing reduction to keep earlier pressure meaningful. In a long fight, manage pools as carefully as health.
strategy.mistakes: Do not unload every tool at once. Do not assume summon timing from a remembered rotation without checking the current fight. Do not let the desire to keep pressure moving stop you from making a necessary reset.
